mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.2% signals aggressive monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as investors shift capital from bonds to stocks.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 8.5% indicates labor market slack, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE > 8.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate accelerating consumer demand, driving positive equity returns over 20 trading days as revenue growth accelerates.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST and RSAFS increases fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) during late-cycle contraction signals weakening manufacturing output, reducing corporate profitability and predicting negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, supporting sustained corporate earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of quarters when GDPC1 growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 225.0 indicates accelerating inflation, triggering Fed rate hikes that compress equity valuations and predict negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 225.0.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) with falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market tightening, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth to drive positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during monetary easing cycles reduces the risk-free rate, increasing equity attractiveness and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.2% during easing cycles.
